subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw make a positive Docker sandbox `pidsLimit` the default for existing unset configs, and what opt-out semantics must ship with it?
rationale: The change improves sandbox hardening but intentionally changes an effective default for existing deployments, so automation cannot choose the security-versus-compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Approve default with proof
options.body: Keep the default-on PID cap after schema/type/docs/tests and real Docker proof cover unset, global, agent, and opt-out behavior.

options.title: Keep default unset
options.body: Preserve current upgrade behavior and document operator-configured `pidsLimit` as the hardening path.

options.title: Use opt-in strict mode
options.body: Introduce the PID cap only through a maintainer-approved strict profile or setting if default-on is too risky.

recommendation.title: Approve default with proof
recommendation.body: Keep the default-on PID cap after schema/type/docs/tests and real Docker proof cover unset, global, agent, and opt-out behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected files are CODEOWNERS-secops sandbox surfaces and the unresolved choice is a sandbox security boundary default.
